seed: Right clicking one of several picked rows means those rows, everywhere else in that menu. This walk draws two rectangles, picks both, right clicks ONE of them and turns it into a picture, and checks that BOTH came out as pictures: the proof is a marquee over the rectangle that was never right clicked, which used to refuse and now takes a piece out. It also checks that the question said so first, in the plural, and that ONE undo takes the whole batch back.

steps.note: two rectangles side by side, both still shapes: three rows in the layers list with the Background
the row menu opened on one of two picked rows still offers 'Turn Into Picture…', and it is about both of them

THE POINT OF THE QUESTION: it reads 'Turn both shapes into pictures?' and says they become pixels so a marquee can cut a piece out of them, that the shapes stop being editable, and that ONE undo puts them all back. It does NOT name one rectangle, which is what it used to do while changing two. Nothing has changed yet
both rows are pictures now and the canvas is identical: two rectangles, same place, same colour, three rows. Compare doc-1-two-rectangles with doc-4-both-turned

THE POINT: the marquee is over 'Rectangle', the row that was NEVER right clicked, and the key took a piece out of it with no refusal at all. Before this change that press raised 'Cannot delete a piece - Only a picture can have a piece taken out', because only the row under the pointer had been turned. The left third of the left rectangle is gone
one undo puts the piece back, the SECOND takes both rectangles back to being shapes: turning two is ONE step, not two. Compare doc-6-both-back with doc-1-two-rectangles

steps.says: Only a picture can have a piece taken out

steps.note: THE OTHER HALF: after that one undo, the row that WAS right clicked refuses the marquee again, so it is a shape again too. One undo really took both back rather than half of them

THE RULE THIS MUST NOT BREAK: with only 'Rectangle 2' picked, the question names it - 'Turn “Rectangle 2” into a picture?' - and says the shape stops being editable, singular. A row outside a selection still acts on that row alone

steps.says: Only a picture can have a piece taken out

steps.note: and 'Rectangle' was left alone by it: the marquee over the left rectangle still refuses, because only the one row picked was turned
